high.title: Latest Food Commodity Prices: Chicken Prices Rise, Rice Remains Stable
high.summary: Key food commodity prices moved mixed on July 19, 2026, according to Bank Indonesia's Strategic Food Price Information Center (PIHPS). Green cayenne pepper rose the most at 5.26% to IDR 53,000/kg, while fresh chicken meat surged 3.92% to IDR 38,450/kg. These price movements are relevant inflation indicators watched closely by Bank Indonesia and investors tracking consumer price trends.

high.title: Bulog Chief Reveals Fate of Rice Food Assistance Program Continuation into July 2026
high.summary: Bulog Director General Ahmad Rizal Ramdhani confirmed the government's rice food assistance program (10kg per recipient) will continue, as Bulog's current rice stock is sufficient. However, distribution is pending a formal assignment from the National Food Agency (Bapanas), which is awaiting the release of a supplementary budget (ABT) from the Ministry of Finance. This has implications for government spending, Bulog's operational outlook, and rice market supply dynamics.

high.title: Anwar Ibrahim Reveals Malaysian Civil Servant Pension Funds Lost in Indonesian Startup eFishery
high.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that KWAP (Malaysia's civil servant pension fund) invested nearly RM 200 million (approximately IDR 860 billion) in Indonesian aquaculture startup eFishery, which engaged in financial statement fraud. The scandal involved manipulation of financial reports that deceived even internationally certified auditors, causing significant losses to Malaysian public sector retirees. This case further damages Indonesia's startup investment credibility and raises serious concerns about corporate governance in the Indonesian tech ecosystem.

high.title: MSCI Tightens Screening Methodology for Stocks with Extreme Price Increases
high.summary: Global index provider MSCI has updated and tightened its screening methodology for stocks experiencing Extreme Price Increases (EPI), effective from the August 2026 Index Review. Under the new rules, stocks flagged as EPI with a Foreign Inclusion Factor (FIF) of 0.75 or above will be exempt from EPI screening and remain eligible for the Standard Index, while those below 0.75 face stricter inclusion conditions. This directly impacts Indonesian stocks listed on MSCI indices, as any extreme price movement could trigger reclassification and affect foreign investor flows.

high.title: IHSG Closes Higher at 6,175 Heading into the Weekend
high.summary: Indonesia's composite stock index (IHSG) closed up 67 points or 1.10% at 6,175 on Friday, July 17, 2026, recovering from an opening at 6,112. Total transaction value reached IDR 14.79 trillion with 28.48 billion shares traded, signaling solid market participation heading into the weekend.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya: Tax Incentive of 0% for 50 Years for Investors in Indonesia International Financial Center Still Under Discussion
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa confirmed that the government has not yet finalized the duration or rate of tax incentives for investors entering the Indonesia International Financial Center (PFII), with discussions still ongoing. He emphasized that any incentive structure will comply with the global minimum tax rule of 15%, meaning rates cannot go below that threshold. This is a significant policy development for international investors considering Indonesia as a financial hub.

high.title: Purbaya on Rating Agencies: 'It's Not That We Don't Trust Them, But...' — Defends Indonesia's Economic Fundamentals After Mixed Assessments
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya pushed back on negative sovereign ratings from Moody's and Fitch, pointing to S&P's stable outlook as evidence that Indonesia's economic fundamentals are stronger than portrayed. His comments signal government confidence in the country's fiscal position despite diverging assessments from major rating agencies. This is relevant for bond investors and those monitoring Indonesia's sovereign credit risk.

high.title: State-Owned Export Entity DSI Claims to Manage US$10 Billion – Danantara CEO Speaks Out
high.summary: Danantara Indonesia CEO Rosan Roeslani confirmed that Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia (DSI) has consolidated US$10.5 billion in export foreign exchange data since launching on June 1, 2026, by integrating data from Customs, Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy into a single platform. This marks a significant shift in Indonesia's export monitoring capability, enabling the government to track export volumes, departure ports, tax payments, and reported prices in real time. The initiative has major implications for exporters and businesses engaged in commodity trade, as under-invoicing and transfer pricing practices are now under closer government scrutiny.

high.title: Single-Channel Export Scheme Through DSI to Launch September 1 – Danantara CEO Explains Mechanism
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has set September 1, 2026 as the launch date for Indonesia's single-channel export scheme through DSI, with Danantara CEO Rosan Roeslani clarifying that DSI will act as a sole selling agent while private exporters can still conduct direct sales. The primary objective is to detect and curb under-invoicing and transfer pricing in export contracts, particularly those with unfixed long-term pricing, by benchmarking reported prices against market reference prices. This policy represents a major structural change to Indonesia's export regime and could significantly impact commodity exporters, mining companies, and palm oil producers listed on the stock exchange.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Says No Plans Yet to Cut Defense Budget
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa stated that there are currently no concrete plans to cut Indonesia's defense budget, despite President Prabowo's earlier indication that austerity measures could extend to the defense sector. Purbaya noted the budget deficit remains manageable and cuts would only be considered if fiscal conditions deteriorate further. This provides short-term reassurance to defense-related industries and signals that overall government austerity, while ongoing, is being applied selectively.

high.title: RUU PFII (Indonesian International Financial Center Bill) Approved, To Be Ratified into Law at DPR Plenary Session Tomorrow
high.summary: Commission XI of the DPR and the government have agreed to bring the Indonesian International Financial Center (PFII) Bill to a plenary session for ratification on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. The bill, which comprises 10 chapters and 73 articles, was finalized with the presence of Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa. This legislation is significant as it establishes a formal legal framework for Indonesia's international financial center, potentially attracting major foreign investment and reshaping the country's capital markets landscape.

high.title: Antam Gold Price Falls Again to This Level
high.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices dropped another Rp 4,000 per gram, now sitting at Rp 2,610,000 per gram, continuing a weakening trend since the end of last week. Over the past week, prices have ranged between Rp 2,614,000 and Rp 2,655,000 per gram, while the monthly range sits between Rp 2,606,000 and Rp 2,703,000. This continued decline is relevant to Indonesian retail investors who use gold as a safe-haven asset and inflation hedge.

high.title: IHSG Closes Higher at 6,231 Level
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed up 0.91% at 6,231.78 on Monday, July 20, 2026, with 399 stocks advancing and 210 declining. Total transaction value reached Rp 17.1 trillion across 35.568 billion shares traded. This marks a continued upward trend following Friday's 1.10% gain to 6,175.54.

high.title: Finance Minister: Business Activities at Indonesia International Financial Center (PFII) to Use Foreign Currency
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa confirmed that all business activities within the planned Indonesia International Financial Center (PFII) will be conducted in foreign currency, with English as the operating language, as part of the draft PFII Law set to be ratified on July 21, 2026. The law also includes special provisions for golden visas, immigration, employment, licensing, and residency to boost Indonesia's competitiveness as an international financial hub. This regulatory development is significant for investors as it signals Indonesia's push to deepen capital markets and attract global investment.

medium.title: President Prabowo Pushes Back Against Critics Who Say Rice Prices Are Too Expensive
medium.summary: President Prabowo Subianto defended current domestic rice prices, arguing that farmers deserve fair income and challenging critics to grow rice themselves. The government indicated it is ready to provide land through the military (TNI) and the Ministry of Agriculture for those who wish to farm. This signals the government's continued stance against rice price suppression, which is relevant for agricultural sector investors and food security policy watchers.

medium.title: Airlangga Says Indonesia Can Become an AI Development Hub — Here's Why
medium.summary: Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto reaffirmed Indonesia's ambition to be an active player — not merely a consumer — in the global AI and digital economy landscape, speaking at the founding meeting of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO). Indonesia aims to shape AI governance and development globally, positioning itself as a key digital economy actor. This is significant for investors in Indonesia's tech and digital infrastructure sectors.

medium.title: MSME Products Can Now Enter Modern Retail Chains Without Administrative Registration Fees
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of MSMEs and the Indonesian Retail Business Association (Aprindo) have signed a partnership agreement to waive listing fees for MSMEs supplying products to modern retail networks, covering over 500 retail companies. This initiative aims to help qualified small businesses expand beyond local markets into modern retail, hospitality, industry, and digital commerce channels. The policy lowers barriers for MSMEs and could significantly boost product distribution and sales volumes across formal retail sectors.

medium.title: Tax Directorate General Strengthens Taxpayer Compliance Monitoring with Web Scraping and Law Enforcement Cooperation
medium.summary: Indonesia's Directorate General of Taxation (DJP) has issued Circular Letter SE-8/PJ/2026 outlining a strengthened taxpayer compliance monitoring framework using both field-based and non-field data collection methods. Non-field methods include digital technology tools such as web scraping to identify potential tax subjects and objects without physical visits. This regulatory tightening signals increased scrutiny for businesses and individuals, with potential implications for tax compliance costs and enforcement actions across sectors.

medium.title: MSCI Tightens Rules for Stocks with Extreme Price Increases, Effective August 2026 Index Review
medium.summary: Global index provider MSCI is tightening its screening methodology for stocks flagged with Extreme Price Increases (EPI), with the new rules taking effect at the August 2026 Index Review. Stocks flagged as EPI with a Foreign Inclusion Factor (FIF) of 0.75 or higher will be exempt from EPI screening and remain eligible for the Standard Index, while those with FIF below 0.75 face stricter scrutiny. Indonesian stocks with unusual price surges and low foreign inclusion could be impacted by inclusion or exclusion decisions.

medium.title: PT Pos Indonesia's Financial Difficulties Behind Delayed Sukuk Payment of IDR 24.11 Billion
medium.summary: State-owned PT Pos Indonesia clarified that it has not defaulted on its Sukuk Ijarah Series A-C payment of IDR 24.11 billion, but has formally requested a payment deferral due to liquidity constraints. The company has notified all relevant parties through official mechanisms as required. This raises concerns about the financial health of the state-owned enterprise and may have implications for sukuk investors and the broader Indonesian fixed income market.

medium.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Responds to MBG (Free School Meal) Budget Cuts
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa acknowledged that the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) is planning to reduce its budget for the Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) free school meal program, though the exact cut amount has not yet been determined. Purbaya plans to meet with BGN leadership this week to discuss the revised strategy for program implementation through year-end. The potential budget reduction may affect food suppliers, catering businesses, and agricultural commodity demand linked to this large-scale government nutrition program.

medium.title: PT Pos Indonesia Has a New President Director
medium.summary: PT Pos Indonesia (Persero) has announced M. Iskandar Kunaefi as its new President Director, replacing Daud Joseph, based on shareholder decree No. 343/2026. The company also restructured its board of directors, splitting the Director of Finance and Risk Management role into two separate positions. As a state-owned enterprise (BUMN), leadership changes at Pos Indonesia signal potential strategic shifts in its logistics and financial services operations.

medium.title: Spain's 2026 World Cup Prize Money: Nearly Rp 1 Trillion
medium.summary: Spain won the 2026 FIFA World Cup, defeating Argentina 1-0 in the final, earning a prize of USD 51 million (approximately Rp 913.97 billion at Rp 17,921/USD). FIFA distributed a record total of USD 871 million across 48 participating teams, over USD 100 million more than previous tournaments following lobbying by European football federations. This article also implicitly reflects the current USD/IDR exchange rate of Rp 17,921, which is relevant context for Indonesian investors monitoring Rupiah performance.

medium.title: The Secret Behind a Modern Batik Business Generating Hundreds of Millions in Revenue
medium.summary: Ergy Adhitama, 33, built his batik business 'Bonolo' from an initial capital of just Rp 10 million, growing it over eight years to employ over 30 people and generate hundreds of millions of rupiah in monthly revenue. The business targets the office-wear segment, betting on sustained demand as long as formal work culture persists in Indonesia. This story highlights opportunities within Indonesia's traditional craft and fashion industry for small-to-medium enterprise (SME) investors.

medium.title: IHSG Strengthens to 6,228 Amid Foreign Selling Pressure in Session I
medium.summary: IHSG gained 0.86% to 6,228.91 by the close of the first trading session on Monday, July 20, despite net foreign selling dominating early trading. Transaction volume reached 20.09 billion shares valued at Rp 8.27 trillion in the morning session. The index's resilience despite foreign outflows suggests strong domestic buying support.

medium.title: DEWA Expands Business Portfolio; ASII Launches Rp 8 Trillion Buyback Program
medium.summary: IHSG closed up 1.10% at 6,175.54 on Friday, July 17, led by major banking stocks BBCA, BBRI, and BMRI, while the financial sector surged 2.34% as the top-performing sector. Foreign investors recorded net buying of Rp 725.11 billion on the regular market, signaling positive sentiment. However, US markets closed lower with the Dow Jones falling 0.77%, S&P 500 down 1.01%, and Nasdaq declining 1.40%, which may influence Monday's trading sentiment.
